--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.topological_overlap()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Compute the topological overlap matrix (TOM). twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.topological_overlap()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Compute the topological overlap matrix (TOM). title: >- [Graph.topological_overlap()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Compute the topological overlap matrix (TOM). page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Compute the topological overlap matrix (TOM). ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L38514-L38651){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.topological_overlap(return_dict=False) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Topological overlap matrix](../assets/graphs/topological-overlap.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="A five-gene network: a diamond G1 to G4 with G5 hanging off G4. G1 and G4 are not linked but share the two neighbors G2 and G3, drawn in the accent color, so their topological overlap is 2 over min(2, 3) + 1, that is 0.67. The table is the full symmetric matrix with 1 on the diagonal and the G1, G4 entries highlighted." width="100%"} For each pair of nodes `(i, j)`, the topological overlap measures how much they share the same neighbors, normalized by the less-connected node's degree: `TOM(i, j) = (|N(i) ∩ N(j)| + a_ij) / (min(k_i, k_j) + 1 - a_ij)` where `a_ij` is 1 if `(i, j)` is an edge, `k` is degree, and `N` is the neighbor set. Diagonal entries are 1.0. This is the standard TOM from WGCNA (weighted gene co-expression network analysis), widely used in genomics for clustering genes into co-expression modules. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, return the TOM as a nested dictionary. Otherwise store each node's row as a `topological_overlap` node attribute and return `self` for chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict or Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A `{node_id: {node_id: tom_value}}` nested dictionary, both levels in the order of `get_node_ids()`, or `self`, with each node's `topological_overlap` attribute a list of `{"node": node_id, "overlap": tom_value}` records, largest first (ties in node ID order), the node itself included. ::: ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~overlap_similarity`) : Shared neighbors over the smaller neighborhood. [](`~jaccard_similarity`) : Shared neighbors over all neighbors. [](`~cmty_louvain`) : Find communities, as WGCNA finds modules. ## Examples {.doc-examples} `A` and `B` are joined and share their one other neighbor, so their overlap is `1.0`. `A` and `D` aren't joined but share `C`, `D`'s only neighbor, so theirs is $1 / (1 + 1)$, one shared neighbor over one more than the smaller degree: ::: {#a2433573 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph.from_edges( [("A", "B"), ("A", "C"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "D")] ) label = graph.get_label_from_id tom = graph.topological_overlap(return_dict=True) row = tom[graph.get_id_from_label("A")] dict(sorted((label(n), t) for n, t in row.items())) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {'A': 1.0, 'B': 1.0, 'C': 1.0, 'D': 0.5} ``` ::: ::: ### A link counts as sharing `friends()` links 24 members of two clubs in a made-up town, a chess club and a climbing club, who are friends. Hugo and Tara are a couple, and each has the other and the same four friends. Mara and Pablo aren't friends, but have the same three. The Jaccard index counts only shared friends, so it scores Mara and Pablo higher, while the topological overlap counts the couple's own link as one more thing they share: ::: {#c120950d .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} friends = ec.friends() node = friends.get_id_from_label tom = friends.topological_overlap(return_dict=True) jaccard = friends.jaccard_similarity() { f"{a}-{b}": ( tom[node(a)][node(b)], round(jaccard[node(a)][node(b)], 2) ) for a, b in [("Hugo", "Tara"), ("Mara", "Pablo")] } ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` {'Hugo-Tara': (1.0, 0.67), 'Mara-Pablo': (0.75, 1.0)} ``` ::: ::: Without `return_dict=True`, each person's row is stored as a `topological_overlap` node attribute, largest first: ::: {#f5ca4b6e .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} friends = friends.topological_overlap() friends.get_node_df().select("label", "topological_overlap").head(3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: Colored by their overlap with Hugo, Tara stands out from everyone else: ::: {#747b163f .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} label = friends.get_label_from_id hugo = tom[node("Hugo")] others = {label(n): t for n, t in hugo.items() if label(n) != "Hugo"} friends = friends.set_node_attrs("like_hugo", others) friends.plot(color_by="like_hugo", label_by="label", seed=8) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: [Similarity and link prediction](../user-guide/similarity.qmd#neighborhood-similarity) compares the topological overlap with the overlap coefficient.
